name: DF-16 (CSS-11) on its WS2500 10x10 transporter-erector-launcher

published.source: en.wikipedia 'WS2500' infobox (its picture is reference [T1], captioned 'WS2500 with DF-16'): 10x10, 15.5 x 3.05 x 2.97 m. The 2.97 m is the same figure the WS2400 article gives and is taken as a cab height. zh.wikipedia DF-16 infobox: the round about 11.4 m long, 1.2 m diameter.

references.name: [T2] Dongfeng-16.JPG, 2015 parade, starboard broadside (hand trace)
references.note: THE MEASURING PHOTO. Seen from starboard (nose right), from roughly 30 m across a junction, so near side-on but not orthographic: the far-side wheels show shifted toward the picture's middle and anything on the centre line (the shell's crown) is about 5 % further away than the near body side. Scale: front of the bumper x 1005 to the tail x 150 (the tail itself is behind leaves; taken 0.18 m behind the last tyre as [T1] shows) = 855 px = the published 15.5 m, 55.16 px/m. Ground y 517 (tyre bottoms). Cross-checks: tyre 86 px = 1.56 m; cab roof y 344 = 3.14 m against the published 2.97 m (5.7 % high, NOT fitted); shell x 182-838 = 11.9 m against an 11.4 m round. The camouflaged vehicle cannot be masked from the trees, so the outline is a HAND TRACE (outline_m) of the near-side profile; below 0.9 m the photograph shows far-side wheels and shadow and is left out (window_m), as are the cab-roof clutter, the mirrors and the tail fitting hidden by leaves (ignore_m). Advisory, not gated.

references.name: [T1] DF-16 Ballistic Missile 20170919.jpg, Beijing Military Museum, starboard front quarter
references.source: Wikimedia Commons 'DF-16 Ballistic Missile 20170919.jpg', 1280 x 853 thumb
references.note: For the reviewer and for every detail the broadside cannot show: the cab front, the box behind the cab, the shell's width against the body's, the skirts and arches, tyres, steps, lamps. Wears camouflage and a star; the model is plain green.

must_show: 10x10 with the axles 2 + 3: two under and just behind the cab (2.5 m apart), a 5 m gap, three close together aft (1.9 m apart); big lugged tyres about 1.56 m, flush with the body sides (side view, x +4.41 +1.93 / -3.04 -4.92 -6.79)

ONE full-width forward-control crew cab ahead of the first axle (not a split cab: the references show no missile nose between cab halves), roof at 3.14 m; two-pane windscreen with a centre pillar leaning back, a quarter window round each corner, two doors with windows and a narrow rear window per side, a belt crease with the lower sides tucked in

cab front: black grille with a V lower edge between two bar-guard frames, guarded amber lamps at the corners, a deep bumper standing forward of the cab with guarded lamp clusters, folding step ladders under the cab ([T1])
the long arched shell over the round, narrower than the body, from 0.6 m ahead of the tail to behind the cab, crown 3.53 m, with hoops at x -5.6, -0.4 and +3.0
the shell's long pointed nose cone (x +3.0 to +4.7) lying over the box behind the cab, its tip at the cab's rear roof edge

the raised louvred box behind the cab (x +2.5 to +4.45, top 3.06 m, a 0.15-0.2 m gap between it and the cab's rear wall) with two columns of slots on the side at its front top (corrected after review: [T2] shows its aft end at +2.49, not +3.1)

slab body sides the full 3.05 m width with flat shoulders either side of the shell, top edge 2.85 m with a handrail line along it; a deep skirt between the second and third axles; trapezoid arches over the three rear axles with fender panels hanging between the tyres
doors, a small rounded port and handles on the body side; an equipment box under the frame between the first and second axles ([T1])
mirrors on tall tube frames at the cab's front corners; a handrail and two covered domes on the cab roof
a trunnion fitting on the tail above the body, behind the shell's rounded rear end ([T1], small)
not_confirmed: the round itself (inside the shell in both photographs): no stage diameters, no fins, no re-entry vehicle are drawn
how the shell opens and the round is raised: no 'podelev' is made (the current model has none either), no erector arm, no launch table
stabiliser jacks: neither photograph shows one that can be identified (the box between axles 1 and 2 is drawn as a plain box)
the plan view: no top or front reference exists; the shell's half width (0.95 m) and the 0.57 m shoulders are estimated from [T1]
the tail: its end and the trunnion fitting are behind leaves in [T2] and tiny in [T1]
the port side (both photographs are from starboard): mirrored
heights of centre-line parts are read straight off [T2] with no perspective correction (the crown may be 0.1 m higher)
the published 15.5 m may be the bare chassis; the tyre size is not published (1.56 m is measured)
the cab roof plan, the hatches under the covered domes, the underside
